sections.html:
North of Charleston County, Berkeley stretches across Lowcountry flatland and is counted within the Charleston metro. Headcount hit 229,861 at the 2020 enumeration, up 29.2 percent from 177,843 ten years earlier, spread over 85,539 households and 93,623 housing units. Goose Creek has the most people, Moncks Corner holds the county government, and Hanahan plus a slice of Summerville sit inside the borders.

Real Property Services carries more than 110,000 properties on its rolls, and each gets an October bill. Plenty of acreage here is swamp, forest or protected land. An owner with a tract near Cypress Gardens or the Wee Tee area is holding something quite unlike a Goose Creek subdivision lot, and the assessment class may differ to match.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax
sections.html:
Three desks handle one tax bill. Real Property Services puts values on land and buildings. The Auditor posts the calendar and takes business personal property returns. The Treasurer takes the money, then splits it among the county, the towns, the school districts and the special taxing districts.

OfficeWhat it handlesWhere to reach it
AuditorDue dates, business personal property1003 Highway 52, Moncks Corner 29461, (843) 719-4309
Real Property ServicesValues, appeals, legal residence rate(843) 719-4061, same administration building
TreasurerCollection and distributionBerkeley County government website

The online payment site runs on PayPal and tacks on a convenience charge. Berkeley County never sees that charge, so walking in or mailing a check is the cheaper route.

Berkeley bills real estate after the tax year ends. Notices go out in October, and payment is due on January 15 of the next year. A January 15 that lands on a weekend or holiday rolls forward to the next business day. For mail, only the postmark matters: stamped on or before the due date means on time.

From January 16 the penalties start piling on. The statute adds 3 percent at the start, another 7 percent from February 2, and a final 5 percent from March 17. Once March 17 is behind you, the treasurer may issue an execution for the unpaid tax, the penalties and the costs.

There is one narrow escape hatch. Suppose the house changed hands during the tax year and the buyer never got a notice in time. In that case the treasurer is directed to waive penalties. Anyone who recently bought or sold should confirm which mailing address the county holds.

Once March 16 passes without payment, the bill is delinquent and the Delinquent Tax Department takes over. That office mails certified notices with restricted delivery. It organizes and conducts the auctions of land and mobile homes, with notices running in the Post and Courier. After an auction it researches title and prepares the deed.

A completed auction is not always the end. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within twelve months of the sale. Interest on the winning bid starts at 3 percent for the first quarter and rises to 12 percent by the fourth, so each quarter of delay costs more.

Every property in South Carolina is reappraised on a five-year rhythm. Berkeley's program years are 1981, 1985, 1999, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. Appraisers aim for fair market value, and millage for each taxing body comes out of its budget divided by the combined assessments.

Real Property Services answers appeals of its own numbers and appears for the county at the Board of Assessment Appeals and, beyond that, the South Carolina Administrative Law Court. The clock starts when your notice is mailed. You get 90 days to object in writing, then 30 days from the assessor's reply to take it to the board.

  • Say in your letter which value or ratio you dispute.
  • A conference is normally set within about 30 days of your request for one.
  • If the board rules against you, the Administrative Law Court is the next step, also within 30 days.

Phone the office to learn which program year applies to your parcel and what your own notice says.

sections.h2: The 4 percent rate when a house changes hands
sections.html:
Nobody gets the 4 percent legal residence rate automatically. Berkeley County wants an application from buyers and from anyone who changed a deed. Real Property takes applications from new buyers who plan to live in the home, from owners who added or dropped a name, from people who created a life estate or a trust, and from households that lost an owner. The deadline for the coming bill is January 15.

Current recipients stay put unless something changes, and the breakdown shows on each yearly bill. That same office looks at agricultural use, rollback taxes, builder and HOA classifications, and the Commercial ATI exemption.

When you sell, assume your buyer starts over with a new application. Without the 4 percent rate, state law taxes a home at 6 percent, and that higher rate is what shows up in a payoff if nobody ever filed.

sections.h2: Paperwork worth pulling before you list
sections.html:
Sellers in Berkeley County save time by collecting a few documents early. Find your most recent tax bill, since it shows the breakdown and whether the 4 percent rate is applied. Dig out the notice from the last reappraisal, which tells you the assessed value and the date your appeal window opened. Write down the dates when a deed changed names, because ownership changes are what trigger new legal residence applications.

If the property includes acreage, ask Real Property how the land is classified. Agricultural use can bring rollback taxes when the use changes, and a buyer's lender or attorney will ask about it. Keeping the Auditor and Real Property on the same mailing address stops bills from drifting to an old owner.

sections.h2: Selling a Berkeley County house with tax due
sections.html:
A sale does not have to wait for the delinquent process. In most deals the title company or attorney pays the tax from your proceeds, which stops penalties from growing and keeps the property off the auction list.

  1. Request a written payoff from the Treasurer or the Delinquent Tax Department, dated for your expected closing day.
  2. Check with Real Property that the owner name and mailing address are current.
  3. Hand the payoff to whoever runs the closing so it appears on the settlement statement.
  4. Tell the buyer to apply for the 4 percent rate once the deed is recorded.

A cash sale to Cash Home Buyers removes the repair list and the showings from the picture. We purchase Berkeley County houses as they are, including inherited homes and homes with tenants. Share the address, the latest tax notice and your timeline, and we will give you a straight answer.

If a sale has already taken place on the property, mention that too. The redemption window and the interest quarter you are in will shape the numbers, and the county's Delinquent Tax Department can tell you the exact cost on a given day.

faqs.q: When are Berkeley County, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 of the year after the October billing. A postmark on or before that date counts for mailed payments, and a weekend due date slides to the next business day.

faqs.q: Where is the Berkeley County Auditor's office?
faqs.a: 1003 Highway 52, Moncks Corner, SC 29461, phone (843) 719-4309. Real Property Services picks up at (843) 719-4061.

faqs.q: How do I get the 4 percent rate on a Berkeley County home?
faqs.a: File an application with Berkeley County Real Property once you own a home you will live in. Existing recipients only reapply after a change, and the cutoff is January 15.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Berkeley County value?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the mailing of the notice to file a written objection. After the assessor replies, another 30 days to reach the board.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Berkeley County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes, penalties and costs get paid out of the proceeds at closing. Request a payoff dated for your closing day.
